edges.description: The knockout directly demonstrates derepression of normally silenced non-rod genes in photoreceptors on loss of SAMD7.
The mouse does not reproduce the human cone-predominant macular dystrophy: the phenotype is rod-centred (ectopic S-opsin and rod dysfunction), and the murine retina has no macula.
edges.limitations: The mouse retina lacks a macula, so a macular dystrophy cannot form, and the Samd7-null phenotype is dominated by rod photoreceptor dysfunction rather than the cone/macular involvement that defines the human disease.

edges.description: Loss of zebrafish samd7 derepresses short-wavelength cone genes in cones, a photoreceptor-subtype-specific instance of the derepression node, though the affected gene set and cone-subtype biology differ from human.
edges.limitations: Zebrafish cone-subtype identity and the specific repressed gene set differ from the human retina, and the zebrafish has no macula, so the model speaks to the derepression step rather than the human macular phenotype.

nodes.description: Generalized (peripheral) cone dysfunction, demonstrated as mildly to moderately reduced cone-driven (light-adapted) responses on full-field electroretinography, was present in six of eight affected individuals; two had isolated macular dystrophy with normal global cone function.

nodes.description: In Samd7-null animal models, loss of SAMD7 derepresses genes normally silenced in a given photoreceptor subtype (for example ectopic non-rod gene and S-opsin expression in rods), reflecting failure of SAMD7-dependent fine-tuning of the CRX-driven photoreceptor gene program. Whether the same derepression underlies the human macular/cone phenotype is not established (see the attached human-model-mismatch discussion).

nodes.description: SAMD7 is a CRX-regulated transcriptional corepressor and a component of PRC1 that normally restrains CRX-dependent transcription in photoreceptors. Disease-associated loss of SAMD7 reduces this repressive activity, as shown directly for a SAM-domain missense variant in a CRX-dependent reporter assay.

nodes.description: The clinical consequence in humans is a bilateral macular dystrophy with cone photoreceptor involvement concentrated in the macula; generalized cone dysfunction beyond the macula is present in most but not all affected individuals. Rod photoreceptor degeneration is not a feature, although a subset of individuals show mild attenuation of dark-adapted (scotopic) rod b-waves on full-field ERG, which the authors read as inner retinal (bipolar-cell) dysfunction rather than rod photoreceptor loss.
